Behavior Tree region — rebuilt from scratch

One BehaviorTree.CPP XML definition, drawn as real SystemSketch Blocks inside a region that paints only the connective tissue. Tree view in MoveIt Pro's idiom, Process view in Intrinsic Flowstate's grammar, a Blackboard lens with three placements checked against py_trees, and a Dataflow lens that wires proven writers to readers with real connections. Built on main at 6e55e902, tldraw 5.3.2, 2026-09-05.

What changed, and why it was rebuilt

The scrapped build drew its own node cards inside a single custom shape — a second canvas beside tldraw — and matched neither reference. This one follows the rule the wireframe board already used: every node is a real Block (or a small control card, or a value pill), the region owns only the XML and the paint between the nodes, and every gesture on a projected child compiles back into an XML edit. Selecting, dragging, renaming, wiring and inspecting a node is the ordinary Block experience; the tree is one more thing those Blocks can be arranged by.

Blackboard lens against py_trees

MetricValueGate
Keys in the sink rank (reference) and below the tree (candidate)True / TruePASS
Key-pair order agreement with Graphviz0.90≥ 0.90 · PASS
Accessor-relative cross-position RMSE (normalised)0.224reported, not gated
Graphviz orderobject_pose → quality → grip_state → grip_force → home_pose
SystemSketch orderobject_pose → quality → grip_force → grip_state → home_pose

Graphviz's Blackboard edges carry weight=0: they order the sink rank by crossing minimisation but do not pull on positions, so the rank is spread evenly. SystemSketch does the same — an exact one-sided crossing minimum for up to eight keys, ties broken by document order — over a tree whose Blocks are far wider than dot's ellipses, which is what the cross-position error measures. The order agreement is the claim that matters; where it is below 1.0 the remaining pairs are ties in Graphviz's own output between runs.

Decision surface

Done and proved

  • BT.CPP v4 parse, diagnostics and structural edits with path remaps — btcppXml.test.ts.
  • Tree (both directions, two control faces, straight or elbow wires) and Process (both directions, groups, fork/join, Failure lane, Fail, merge) — layout tests plus the captures above.
  • Blackboard lens: rail, table, py_trees placements; writes into the inlet, reads out of the outlet; py_trees comparison above.
  • Dataflow lens: static happens-before analysis, direct cables as real connections, root inputs through an unbundle, residual keys as pills.
  • Authoring: on-canvas “+” with the Add-process menu, inspector structure actions, Delete key, rename through the XML, drag with Tidy, undo as one step each.

Left, and not blocked

  • Portable .tldr export lowers Branch and Loop; the Behavior Tree region is not yet detached to stock shapes (its children already are stock-loadable Blocks and pills).
  • Library drag-and-drop onto a target; today the library inserts under or after the selection with a click.
  • Reparenting an existing card by dragging it onto another wire (the inspector's Move earlier / later and the XML cover reordering).
  • Dark theme pass on the region's paint, and forced-colours.

Needs Zach

  • Card face for the Process view. Default: the Block's simple face (icon, title, Skill). Alternative: a Flowstate-literal face (title, skill row, resource row). Silence keeps the Block.
  • py_trees placement. Default: exact crossing-minimal order spread evenly (what Graphviz does). Alternative: pull each key under the barycentre of its accessors. Silence keeps Graphviz's rule.
  • Merge. Everything is on main in the primary checkout, uncommitted until you say so.

Deliberately not done

  • No runtime controls (Run / Pause / Step) and no fake status: there is no transport to feed them.
  • No ELK for the Process view: Flowstate's grammar is a fixed recursive box model, and owning every gap is what made the overlay above line up.
  • No second graph model: Tree, Process, Blackboard and Dataflow all read the same parsed XML.
